view: Thursday's CEO-exit bar (open 151.01, low 148.80, close 166.19 on 748M shares, about 5.2x the 60-day average) has the shape of a stock-specific selling climax. Friday then gave back the rebound on 2.5x volume, VIX fell 30% on the week, and the AAII and CNN readings are stale and taken before the shock. So this reads as forced, governance-driven distribution that may be nearing climax, not a confirmed market-wide capitulation. Tactical: Wait through the 2026-11-17 print. Strategic: no sentiment objection to Accumulate at plan levels once the chair rules on TB2. Avoid both 'oversold = buy' (weekly RSI 32.5 is not below 30) and any urgency to act before earnings.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 162.85 (Fri 2026-11-13 close, weekend run). next_2_weeks: up = close > 170.99, down = close < 154.71, range between, measured at the close on or before 2026-11-29 (i.e. Fri 2026-11-27). this_quarter: to the last close of Q4 2026 (2026-12-31); next_quarter: to the last close of Q1 2027 (2027-03-31); up = close > 179.14, down = close < 146.57, range between. up+range+down=100.

evidence.point: Outside view: 33 up / 45 range / 22 down (n=258). I cut range by 17 pts because earnings on 11-17 falls inside the window and daily ATR is 6.1% (structure.atr_daily_pct), so a ±5% band is narrow. I add 16 pts to down for the governance overhang and Friday's failed rebound. Net change from my 11-12 trial view (32/28/40) is small: price held above the climax low, but no fresh sentiment data has come in.

Weekly RSI ≤36 gives 46/23/31 over 2w and 69/0/31 over 13w, but n=13 with overlapping windows, and the 2w drop ≤-15% table has n=4. Treated as weak evidence only. It is the main reason next_quarter up sits at 43 rather than near the 50 base. None of these samples contains a CEO departure.

Nov 12: 747.7M shares vs 60d average 144.9M (tv_chart_owner.daily_avg_volume_60d_shares), about 5.2x. Gap to 148.80, then close at 166.19, +11.7% off the low. This is the classic selling-climax shape, and it suggests forced sellers were absorbed that day.

Fri Nov 13 opened at 169.905 (+2.2% gap), was rejected at 170.00 and closed 162.85, below Thursday's close, on 2.5x average volume (structure.today_volume_vs_60d_avg). Follow-through failed, which fits continued distribution rather than a finished capitulation. The low of 158.39 still held well above 148.80.

The week traded 2.34B shares, with Mon/Tue already at 463M/429M before the shock (tv_chart_owner.volume_mon_tue_shares, structure.volume_spike_ratio_mon 3.2). Heavy selling began before the CEO news, so this is more than a one-day panic. The weekly close of 162.85 sits only about 45% up the 148.80-179.92 range, not at the high: no weekly reversal bar.

VIX was 19.29, down 30.31% on the week, while NVDA fell 12.75%. HY OAS was 3.2 and tightening, and RSP +4.04% vs SPY -2.65% over 1m. Broad-market fear is easing while NVDA sells off, so the fear is stock-specific and megacap-rotation driven, not a market-wide washout. Contrarian 'extreme fear' readings therefore apply to NVDA less than they appear to.

STALE (week ending 2026-11-04, partial read): bullish 34.1, bearish 48.4, spread -14.3; historical averages are bull 37.5 / bear 31.5. Bearish has been above average for 39 weeks. That is mildly contrarian-bullish, but it predates the CEO exit, and a 39-week run of above-average bearishness has not worked as a timing signal. Weighted low.

STALE (secondary reports, CNN page not readable): 20 'Extreme Fear' on 2026-11-06, 'Fear' with no value on 2026-11-11. Fear was already easing before NVDA's worst day, which matches the VIX picture. No reading after event_cutoff_utc 2026-11-13T21:00Z. Unknown, not neutral.

Not available (deferred, paid data). Without it I cannot see the earnings implied move (is the ~6% daily ATR already priced?), put/call or skew (are holders already hedged, which would argue capitulation, or not?), or dealer gamma near 150/160/170. This is the single biggest gap for a pre-earnings sentiment call, and it is why confidence is 30 rather than about 45.

Owner bias audit, 'oversold = buy': weekly RSI7 18.35, Stoch RSI 0/0, daily RSI14 24.86, two BBPCT bottom triangles. Stretched, but weekly RSI14 is 32.53, above 30 (weekly_rsi.is_oversold=false), the same trap logged on 2026-11-11. One momentum group: the technical member owns it, so count it once.

Owner bias audit, ATH anchor: 243.37 is -33.1% away (structure.drawdown_from_ath_pct). 'A third off the high' is an anchor, not a valuation. The 0.65/0.618 fibs (161.98/154.53) are drawn from that same anchor, so they share its weakness. Levels should come from the plan, not from distance to the ATH.

Urgency audit: the 12/14 pages that are ok are all price, macro and news. Both sentiment pages are stale and options are deferred. Acting before 11-17 means taking the binary print with the least sentiment visibility of the whole cycle. Waiting costs at most the gap between now and a post-print price, and the 2w drop ≤-15% table (n=4) is not strong enough to justify that urgency.

key_levels.why: Nov 12 climax low. A close below it means the selling climax failed and the distribution is not done.
2w down threshold. The owner's fib 0.618 is at 154.53 (anchor caveat applies).
price_at_call. The fib 0.65 (161.98) and swing label 164.27 are anchors near price: do not treat them as support without volume evidence.
Fri rejection high. Just below 170.99 (2w up threshold) and sma111w 171.42.
Bottom of the unfilled gap 179.92-185.22. A close inside it would mean shock sellers are trapped and sentiment has turned.
ATH: named as an anchor to avoid, not a target.

what_would_change_my_mind: Daily close below 148.80 (Nov 12 climax low, -8.6%) before 2026-11-27. The climax would have failed, so I would raise 2w down to 50 or more. Reachable: 2w -5% 41.0%, -10% 17.1%.

Pullback to 150-158 that holds above 148.80 on daily volume under 290M (2x 60d average). That is a low-volume retest, which confirms capitulation, so I would move 2w up toward 42. Reachable: 2w -5% 41.0%.
Post-earnings close above 179.92 (gap bottom, +10.5%) by 2026-11-27. Sentiment would have flipped, so I would raise this_quarter up to 45 or more. Reachable: 2w +10% 26.2%.

Earnings outcome: an in-line or better guide that is still sold, with a close below 154.71 within two sessions of 11-17, would mean holders are using good news to exit (distribution). I would raise all down buckets by 5-8 pts. Event trigger: the print itself is Expected.

First post-shock AAII reading (week ending 11-18 or 11-25) with bullish above 45 while NVDA is under 170. Retail would be buying the dip too eagerly (complacency), which removes the contrarian support, so I would cut next_quarter up by about 5.
notes_for_chair: Expected: earnings on 2026-11-17 after close, inside the 2w window. Before the print, sentiment says only that the stock is stretched and stock-specific fear is high. After the print, the reaction to the number is the real sentiment test (see triggers). Re-read sentiment and options after the print if possible.

TB2 (CEO departs under legal or regulatory pressure) is not my lane, but it overrides everything here. If TB2 fires, all buying pauses regardless of how capitulation-like the tape looks. Please rule on it before reading my strategic line.

Cross-domain for macro and relative_strength: VIX -30.31% on the week and RSP outperforming SPY while NVDA fell 12.75%. Please confirm this is idiosyncratic and rotation-driven. If so, broad-market extreme-fear readings should not be used as an NVDA bottom signal.
Do not double count: the weekly/daily oscillator readings I cite are the technical member's momentum group. My independent inputs are volume and bar structure, AAII, CNN F&G and VIX.
Both sentiment pages are stale and from before event_cutoff_utc. Options are deferred. Discount my confidence (30) accordingly.
The draft Equity Bottom checklist (not approved, not back-tested) would likely show 'volume climax' as present. Report it as information only.

Pre-mortem: three months later this was badly wrong. Most likely reason: the Nov 12 bar really was the low, the 2022/2025-style rebound (conditional n=4/13) played out, and I underweighted it because the trigger was governance rather than sentiment. Second most likely: governance de-rating persisted and 148.80 broke after a sold earnings beat.
